items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Him and Kidora come from the same home.

ctx.x: But what about your army service? Did you play any music then?

Yeah, I was bugle. I played in the brass band and I played in the dance orchestra. Didn't I tell you about it? I used to go along and watch a fella named Chiff and the brass band parade, watch his fingers. I was fast enough to make the same thing he'd be making, but he told me that wasn't no good. He said, the best thing for you to do is to, I know a little music then, but I didn't know no marches, because Port Royalty was showing me pretty good. But I couldn't get them marches down like I wanted, see. After I…
You say Chiff's been dead. Three years. Three years now. I never met him.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: So, Ori and Johnny Dotson, him. So, they invited me up to play a piece, and I played a piece

ctx.x: You remember some of the other good musicians around here? You said you played in Jack Carey's band. Who were some of the other bands, the other trumpet players you heard when you first came here?

When I first came here? Yeah. Well, Buddy Petit was one of the fellas, Ray and Plinistain. And Kid René. And Louis too, Louis Armstrong. He was cracking them up. But the idea about Louis, he always played off like the Capitol Boat. And going off something, you know, like that. He'd play in brass bands every now and then, but he wasn't exactly with us, because he always looked like a little above that, or some kind of really. Yeah. Big time people would hire him all the time, you know. He'd work with a kid, Ori,…
Louis thought you meant it though, huh, did he? Yeah. Louis thought they were going to hire you in this place?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1971-04-08
items.q: I know the first time I got on the wagon with Kid O'er to make an advertisement for a big dance. They just hired me because I played at the, uh, 25 with them one night

ctx.x: Well, a little bit. And you were with them?

Yeah, I came here from the Army and got right in there with them. They heard me playing, and they just lashed right on to me. I was, I was, I'll come here, but I didn't know many songs, which was playing in civilian life then. I don't know, a lot of Army songs. So, yeah, I, I didn't take me no time to learn them, soon to play stuff. I learned, I know the first time I got on the wagon with Kid O'er to make an advertisement for a big dance. They just hired me because I played at the, uh, 25 with them one night when…
Did you know it's a long way to temporary? Oh, yeah. When did you play that number? In the Army. Oh, yeah.
